title: Serving
tomorrow: first paycheck's in. how much goes to church, if any?

segments.voice: Yesterday was staying when it's hard, and the line was faithful, honestly: stay or leave well, never pretend. Today, the jobs nobody claps for.
screen: `FAITHFUL, HONESTLY.` → `NOW, THE JOBS NOBODY CLAPS FOR.`

segments.voice: A sign-up sheet on a folding table: food pantry, Saturday, hands needed. The first name on it belongs to someone who doesn't even go to that church. Somebody else set out the chairs this morning, made the coffee, and fixed the speaker that buzzed during the hymn. Nobody announced their names. A church that looks effortless from the pew runs on hands like these, and the book of Acts shows it happening.
screen: `FOOD PANTRY: HANDS NEEDED.` → `THE CHAIRS, THE COFFEE.` → `NOBODY CLAPS.`

segments.voice: Early in Acts, the young church in Jerusalem hits a problem. Some widows are being overlooked in the “daily ministration,” the daily sharing of food. The apostles say: “It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.” So they ask the church to choose seven trusted people, “full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom,” for the work, while they give themselves to prayer and “the ministry of the word.” Here's the surprise worth passing on: in the Greek of Acts, ministration, serve and ministry all share one root, diakon. Waiting tables and preaching sit in the same family of words. Two kinds of serving, neither looked down on. Jesus had set the pattern: “For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister.” And Peter's letter hands it to everyone: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.” A steady hand, a good ear, a car, a spare Saturday: grace passing through, meant to be handed on. Churches organize this differently. Some ordain deacons, some keep volunteer lists, some just ask who's free. Whatever the system, a church runs on hands.
screen: `WIDOWS OVERLOOKED.` · `SEVEN CHOSEN FOR THE TABLES.` · `ONE ROOT: DIAKON.` · `EVERY GIFT, HANDED ON.` · then, large: `HANDS NEEDED.`

segments.voice: Do one small job for the place you're in right now: put away a dish, straighten a shoe, wipe a counter. Do it slowly and well, the way someone set out those chairs. If you pray, offer your hands with it.
Serving. Giving your hands, time and gifts to a church's work, in whatever office fits you.
Keep this one: hands needed, tables and the word, one family of serving. Day seventeen forty-eight.
